_doc: Investment-cost model for dc2_s, grounded in the real playbook config (config/playbooks/dc2_s.json, 4 of 4 covered) and the real pillar catalog (config/dc2s_kpi_catalog.json). Companion to config/economics/dc2_s.json. Same {value, basis} discipline as config/investment/saas_premium.json: every figure carries {value, basis}, and a figure computed from two assumed inputs is itself 'assumed' (roi.basis.money()'s weakest-link rule), never 'derived' just because arithmetic was involved.

csm_hourly_cost.basis: assumed: blended fully-loaded CSM/CS-ops hourly cost, same figure as every other vertical's file — CSM cost doesn't vary by vertical the way retention sensitivity does (config/investment/saas_premium.json's own basis sentence).

_playbooks_doc: Grounded in config/playbooks/dc2_s.json's 4 real playbooks. targets_pillars is resolved mechanically (power_of_1.json's attribution.signal_role_to_pillar_role crossed with config/dc2s_kpi_catalog.json's pillar_roles) and cross-checked by hand. estimated_health_point_lift_per_execution is a placeholder ONLY until roi.measured's per-playbook sensitivity (>=5 closed interventions with both a health lift and a revenue outcome) exists for that playbook.

estimated_csm_hours.basis: assumed: thermal-incident triage with the facilities/hardware team + a customer exec update call + resolution follow-through + a wrap-up report, 'escalate' action_class

estimated_cost_per_execution.basis: assumed: estimated_csm_hours (assumed) x csm_hourly_cost (assumed) — both links assumed, so the product is assumed, not derived

estimated_health_point_lift_per_executio.basis: assumed: informal CS-leadership estimate for a resolved thermal incident's effect on P2 (Operational Stability); no dc2_s tenant yet has >=5 closed instances of this playbook with both a measured lift and a revenue outcome — replace with roi.measured's sensitivity figure once one does

estimated_csm_hours.basis: assumed: capacity/GPU-utilization analysis + a pricing proposal for additional hardware + a presentation call + a follow-up, 'offer' action_class

estimated_health_point_lift_per_executio.note: this playbook's expected_outcome is entirely expansion/commercial (expansion_closed, expansion_opportunity, repeat_order) — no health-score outcome type. Left null rather than forced, mirroring saas_premium's expansion_intent_handoff, even though it also touches P3 conceptually via its capacity_pressure trigger role.

estimated_csm_hours.basis: assumed: a hardware-refresh usage review + a renewal/refresh-terms conversation under commercial pressure + a follow-up, 'schedule' action_class

estimated_health_point_lift_per_executio.note: this playbook's trigger role (commercial_pressure) resolves to the 'revenue' pillar_role in power_of_1.json's attribution map, but config/dc2s_kpi_catalog.json's pillar_roles has no 'revenue' entry at all (unlike datacenter_v1, which maps 'revenue' to P1) — there is no pillar to attribute a health-point lift to. This is a real, mechanically-confirmed gap (verified by cross-referencing the attribution map against this catalog directly), not a guess; the playbook still gets real cost figures above since those don't depend on a pillar mapping.

estimated_csm_hours.basis: assumed: qualify the signal + warm handoff to sales, 'notify' action_class — the lightest-touch playbook in this catalog

estimated_health_point_lift_per_executio.note: this playbook's expected_outcome is expansion revenue, not a health-score lift — same shape as saas_premium's expansion_intent_handoff.

_pillars_doc: Pillar-level cost rolls up from the playbooks that target it. A pillar with no targeting playbook is shown as not_covered, not guessed.

P1.name: Deployment Velocity
P1.note: no playbook in config/playbooks/dc2_s.json targets the 'adoption' role this pillar plays — none of the 4 real playbooks fire on a deployment/onboarding-velocity signal (delivery_stall, usage_decline). Absent, not guessed.

P2.name: Operational Stability
P2.note: one playbook covers this pillar, targeting Thermal Management Score (P2-KPI5) specifically — the playbook is literally the thermal-incident response

P3.name: AI Workload Performance
P3.note: one playbook touches this pillar conceptually (capacity_pressure is one of its two trigger roles, and this catalog's own pillar_roles_notes maps AI Workload Performance to 'capacity') but its tracked outcome is expansion revenue, not a health-point lift — see the playbook's own null lift note

P4.name: Channel & Partner Health
P4.note: no playbook in config/playbooks/dc2_s.json targets the 'partner' role this pillar plays — none of the 4 real playbooks fire on a channel/partner signal. Absent, not guessed.

P5.name: Expansion Readiness
P5.note: two playbooks target this pillar; both are grow-lens plays with expansion-revenue outcomes, not health-point lifts — costs reported side by side, not summed, same as saas_premium's P5 rule. refresh_at_risk_save (the protect-lens commercial play) deliberately does NOT target this pillar — see its own note: 'Expansion Readiness' measures growth propensity, not renewal protection, and this vertical has no separate revenue-protection pillar for it to land on instead.

_kpis_doc: KPI-level entries exist only for KPIs a playbook actually names in targets_kpis.

P2-KPI5.name: Thermal Management Score
P2-KPI5.note: inherits its one playbook's cost/lift figures directly; no KPI-specific override authored yet

P5-KPI7.name: Expansion Probability (90d)
P5-KPI7.note: inherits its one playbook's cost figures; no health-point lift (this KPI moves on the expansion-revenue side, not a health score)
